shifts.summary: The first shift was overall moderate in difficulty. Candidates reported attempting between 72 and 80 questions successfully. Reasoning was generally easy with 17–24 good attempts, while General Awareness showed a mixed difficulty and 15–17 good attempts. Quantitative section difficulty varied, with 14–22 good attempts. English difficulty ranged from easy to moderate with 17 good attempts.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Reasoning was the longest part, many statement‑based items. Candidates felt attempts were low.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GA content included current affairs up to 2023 and a few recent items. Scope was limited but questions were straightforward for some.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Math featured advanced problems and some lengthy items, causing time pressure.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English had many passage‑based items and a focus on direct/indirect speech and voice transformation.

shifts.summary: The shift 2 paper was reported overall as moderate in difficulty. Candidates said reasoning was generally easy to moderate, while GA and Quant were moderate and English ranged from easy to moderate. Good attempts varied, with overall attempts reported between 75 and 99. Time pressure was noted in English passages and the math section due to a sectional timer. Some candidates found certain reasoning matrix questions tougher.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: Current affairs made up about 15% of GA, many questions were recent year, and topics included economics, polity, geography and specific articles.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Math paper was lengthy with a sectional timer, formula‑based and advanced topics were prominent, and many candidates could attempt 17‑18 questions.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English had language‑based questions and long passages, which caused some time shortage, but overall candidates found it easier than previous years.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 12 October 2026 comprised three shifts. Shifts 1 and 2 were reported as moderate in overall difficulty, with unofficial good‑attempt ranges of 72–80 and 75–99 respectively. Candidates noted that reasoning and English sections varied from easy to moderate, while General Awareness and Quantitative sections were generally moderate. Shift 3 has no usable analysis yet, and further candidate evidence is required before publishing details. All figures are unofficial; SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: What overall difficulty was reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 12 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shifts 1 and 2 were described as moderate in overall difficulty; shift 3 has no usable analysis yet, so its difficulty cannot be confirmed at this time.

faqs.q: How many questions did candidates reportedly answer correctly on 12 October 2026?
faqs.a: Unofficial reports indicate good attempts of 72–80 for shift 1 and 75–99 for shift 2. No data is available for shift 3 pending further evidence.

faqs.q: Which sections were considered easier or harder on 12 October 2026?
faqs.a: In shift 1, reasoning (17–24 good attempts) and English (17 good attempts) were seen as easier, while General Awareness (15–17) and Quantitative (14–22) varied. Shift 2 showed reasoning generally easy to moderate, General Awareness and Quantitative moderate, and English ranging from easy to moderate.

faqs.q: Was time pressure reported as an issue on 12 October 2026?
faqs.a: Yes, candidates for shift 2 noted time pressure in the English passages and the mathematics section due to a sectional timer.

faqs.q: When will analysis for shift 3 of the 12 October 2026 exam be available?
faqs.a: No usable analysis has been published for shift 3 yet; additional candidate evidence is needed before a review can be released.
